title: Chapter 129 — The Cabin
paragraphs: (Ahab moving to go on deck; Pip catches him by the hand to follow.)

"Lad, lad, I tell you that you must not follow Ahab now. The hour is coming when Ahab would not scare you from him, yet would not have you by him. There is something in you, poor lad, that I feel is too much of a cure for my malady. Like cures like; and for this hunt, my malady becomes my most desired health. Stay down here, where they will serve you as if you were the captain. Aye, lad, you shall sit here in my own screwed chair; you must be another screw to it."
"No, no, no! You don't have a whole body, sir; just use poor me for your one lost leg; only tread on me, sir; I ask no more, so long as I remain a part of you."
"Oh! in spite of a million villains, this makes me a bigot in the fadeless fidelity of man! — and a black! and crazy! — but I think like-cures-like applies to him too; he grows so sane again."

"They tell me, sir, that Stubb once abandoned poor little Pip, whose drowned bones now show white, for all the blackness of his living skin. But I will never abandon you, sir, the way Stubb did him. Sir, I have to go with you."
"If you talk to me like this much more, Ahab's purpose will turn keel-up in him. I tell you no; it cannot be."

"Weep like that, and I will murder you! Take care, for Ahab too is mad. Listen, and you will often hear my ivory foot upon the deck, and still know that I am there. And now I leave you. Your hand! — Met! You are as true, lad, as the circumference to its center. So: God forever bless you; and if it comes to that — God forever save you, come what may."
(Ahab goes; Pip steps one step forward.)

"He stood here this very instant; I stand in his air — but I'm alone. Now if even poor Pip were here I could endure it, but he's missing. Pip! Pip! Ding, dong, ding! Who's seen Pip? He must be up here; let's try the door. What? Neither lock, nor bolt, nor bar; and yet there's no opening it. It must be the spell; he told me to stay here. Yes, and told me this screwed chair was mine. Here, then, I'll sit myself down, against the transom, in the ship's full middle, all her keel and her three masts before me. Here, our old sailors say, in their black seventy-fours (warships of seventy-four guns) great admirals sometimes sit at table and lord it over rows of captains and lieutenants. Ha! What's this? Epaulets! epaulets! The epaulets all come crowding! Pass round the decanters; glad to see you; fill up, monsieurs! What an odd feeling, now, when a black boy's host to white men with gold lace on their coats! — Monsieurs, have you seen one Pip? — a little negro lad, five feet high, hang-dog look, and cowardly! Jumped from a whale-boat once — seen him? No! Well then, fill up again, captains, and let's drink shame upon all cowards! I name no names. Shame upon them! Put one foot upon the table. Shame upon all cowards. — Hush! Up there, I hear ivory — Oh, master! master! I am down-hearted indeed when you walk over me. But here I'll stay, though this stern strikes rocks, and they bulge through, and oysters come to join me."
